description.content:
Connect a new OF account.

Managed capacity is preflighted before creating the of_accounts row; the
sticky assignment is resolved before any upstream client call. The row's
status follows the OF auth state
machine: ``pending → authenticated`` on success, or
``pending → otp_required → authenticated`` when 2FA is in play.

response.name: ``account.already_connected``: an account in this workspace already uses this OnlyFans email. Its id is in ``X-OFMAPI-Account-Id``; sign it in again with ``/retry-auth``.
OF requires the 6-digit OTP. The account is created in the ``otp_required`` state; submit the code via ``POST /v1/accounts/{id}/verify``.

Sign-in ended before OF accepted or rejected the credentials (``account.captcha_failed`` / ``account.sign_in_failed``). The account is left ``authentication_failed``; its id is in ``X-OFMAPI-Account-Id`` for ``/retry-auth``.
Account not found, or ``account.no_pending_otp``: the challenge expired (15 min) or was lost in a restart. Request a new code via ``/reconnect`` or ``/retry-auth``.
Submitting the code ended without an OF verdict (``account.captcha_failed`` / ``account.sign_in_failed``). The challenge stays pending; retry the same code.

description.content:
Hard-disconnect: tear down the OF→NATS bridge, remove from the live
session pool, then delete the row. Idempotent — calling delete on an
already-gone account returns 204 too.

Re-establish the in-memory OF client + WS subscription.

Two-tier strategy:

1. **Cookies tier** — load the saved session data from disk
   and validate by hitting OF's ``/users/me``. If OF accepts the
   cookies, we're done.
2. **Credentials tier** (email_password rows only) — if the
   cookies are dead AND we have a stored email+password from a
   previous successful sign-in, replay ``sign_in()`` against the
   same row. Re-mints a fresh session non-interactively.

Returns 409 when both tiers fail (saved cookies dead and either
we have no stored credentials, or those credentials are also no
longer accepted). The frontend uses 409 as the signal to open the
retry-auth modal so the user can paste fresh creds / cookies.

Historical note: this endpoint used to call ``client.connect()``
and call it a day. ``connect()`` only loads state into memory —
it doesn't actually talk to OF. So a dead session returned 200
here and then exploded on the next real API call. The
``get_me()`` validation is what makes the success signal real.

response.name: The saved session is dead and we couldn't silently replay credentials. The frontend should open the retry-auth modal.
Stored credentials worked, but OF is now asking for an OTP. Submit it via /verify.

description.content:
Re-run sign-in against an existing account row that's NOT authenticated.

Use this when the original ``POST /v1/accounts`` got stuck in
``pending`` / ``authentication_failed`` / ``session_expired`` and
you want to retry with the same (or different) credentials WITHOUT
losing the account_id, webhook subscriptions, or audit history.

Difference from ``POST /v1/accounts/{id}/reconnect``: that one
needs a saved session file on disk. If the initial sign-in
crashed before the session was written, there's nothing to
reconnect to — retry-auth re-runs the full sign-in flow.

Difference from ``DELETE`` then ``POST /v1/accounts``: that gives
you a fresh ``account_id``. Retry-auth keeps the existing one.

response.name: Account is already authenticated; nothing to retry.
Body doesn't match the chosen auth_method.
OTP challenge — submit the code via /verify.
Sign-in ended before OF accepted or rejected the credentials (``account.captcha_failed`` / ``account.sign_in_failed``). The account is left ``authentication_failed``.

description.content:
Report whether this account is on the managed pool or a custom URL.
NEVER returns the plaintext URL — only a redacted host hint.

Set a per-account BYO proxy URL.

Persists the encrypted URL, then immediately re-loads the live OF
client through the new proxy (the customer's explicit will).
If the live-reload fails, the persist still stands and the next
natural reconnect will pick it up — we don't auto-revert.

Revert to the managed pool. Idempotent when the route reload succeeds.

Managed capacity is acquired before clearing BYO. The live session is
then reloaded immediately. A reload failure restores the prior customer
route when possible and returns a sanitized, retryable 503; it is never
reported as an atomic success.

One-shot HTTP GET through the proxy URL → reports back the egress
IP + country + latency. Use ``body.url`` when testing a URL the
customer just pasted (before saving); omit it to test the currently
saved BYO URL on this account.
Get the authenticated user's own information.

Get information about a specific user.

The username can be the OnlyFans username or user ID.

Get inbox conversations.

Set ``pages`` to ``-1`` to fetch all pages (use with caution on large
inboxes — paginate explicitly when in doubt).

Optional filters mirror the upstream client's ``query`` and
``_filter`` arguments: free-text search and a state-based chip
filter respectively.

Filter by chat state — unread / who_tipped / paid / locked / priority / pinned / unread_with_tips (added upstream 2026-05-10) (This can only be one of unread,who_tipped,paid,locked,priority,pinned,unread_with_tips)

Filter by chat state — unread / who_tipped / paid / locked / priority / pinned / unread_with_tips (added upstream 2026-05-10) (This can only be one of unread,who_tipped,paid,locked,priority,pinned,unread_with_tips)

Filter by chat state — unread / who_tipped / paid / locked / priority / pinned / unread_with_tips (added upstream 2026-05-10) (This can only be one of unread,who_tipped,paid,locked,priority,pinned,unread_with_tips)

Mark every conversation in the inbox as read.

Wraps upstream ``BotMethods.mark_all_conversation_as_read()``
(added 2026-05-10 in commit ``62bb3f2``), which POSTs to
OnlyFans' ``/api2/v2/chats/mark-as-read`` endpoint.

No request body. Returns ``{"success": true}`` on success. The
operation is idempotent on OnlyFans' side — calling twice in a row
is safe and the second call is effectively a no-op.

Get messages from a specific conversation.

The ``conversation_id`` is typically the user ID of the other person.

Each message's ``media`` items carry ``downloadUrl`` /
``downloadUrls`` / ``videoQualities`` pointing at our HMAC-signed
proxy (``/v1/accounts/{id}/media/download``), so purchased photos
and videos play from any browser. Locked PPV media the connected
account hasn't bought has ``canView: false`` and no URLs.

``seenByFan`` on the creator's own messages says whether the fan has
seen them.

Reading a chat's messages marks the chat read on OnlyFans, the same
as opening it in the OnlyFans app: its unread count drops to 0 for the
creator's chatters too (verified 2026-10-24). A bot that reads history
before a human answers will clear that chat's unread badge; put it
back with POST /conversations/{id}/mark-unread.

description.content: Pagination cursor: the `cursor` of the previous page

One message of a conversation by ID, with the same typed fields as
the list (``seenByFan``, ``isOpened``, ``canPurchase`` …). 404 when
the conversation has no such message.

OnlyFans has no single-message read. This asks the chat's message
list for the newest message older than ``message_id + 1`` (the list's
``id`` cursor is strict), which is the message itself when it belongs
to this chat.

Unlike the list, this does NOT mark the chat read: OnlyFans only does
that for the newest page. Verified 2026-10-25 on an unread chat; its
unread count and read marker stayed as they were.
Delete a single message from a conversation.
Hide a conversation from the inbox (recoverable).

Send a transient 'typing...' indicator to the fan.

Wraps upstream ``send_typing_indicator`` — uses the WebSocket
channel rather than HTTP. The future awaited upstream is small;
we report success when it resolves without raising.

Mark one conversation read without reading its messages.

The chat's unread count drops to 0 for the creator's chatters too,
the same as opening it in OnlyFans. Wraps OnlyFans'
``POST /chats/{id}/mark-as-read`` (no library method).

Mark one conversation unread again.

Reading a chat's latest messages through this API (GET
/conversations/{id}, the pinned list) marks the chat read on
OnlyFans, which clears the unread badge the creator's chatters work
from. A bot that reads a chat before a human answers can put the
badge back with this call. (Fetching one message by ID does not mark
the chat read.)

OnlyFans has no ``mark-as-unread`` route: it is
``DELETE /chats/{id}/mark-as-read`` (verified 2026-10-25, unread
count 0 → 1). No library method.

List media items exchanged in one conversation.

One item per media object, newest message first, with the carrying
message's ``messageId`` / ``fromUserId`` / ``price`` alongside. Each
item carries ``downloadUrl`` / ``downloadUrls`` / ``videoQualities``
pointing at our HMAC-signed proxy
(``/v1/accounts/{id}/media/download``). Locked PPV media the
connected account hasn't bought has ``canView: false`` and no URLs.

The library has the call but no ``BotMethods`` wrapper:

Send a direct message to a conversation partner.

Either ``text`` or ``media`` must be provided. The recipient must be
in an open chat relationship with the sender (typically: a creator
can DM their subscribers; subscribers can DM creators they sub to).

For paywalled (PPV) messages, set ``price`` > 0. Set ``lockedText``
if the text body itself should also be paywalled (not just media).

Provide exactly one of ``users_list_id`` or ``recipients``. Upstream

Omitting it fires the send immediately.

List the OF-native scheduled-message queue for this account.

OnlyFans runs the scheduler for future-dated mass messages
server-side (see ``POST /mass-messages`` with ``scheduleAt``).
This endpoint is the visibility surface on what's queued — the
items are what OF will fire on its own clock.

Returns the full list. OF doesn't paginate this endpoint and the
queues are small in practice (typically <50 items per account),
so we don't either.

Cancel a queued / scheduled message before OF fires it.

Upstream returns the response body's ``success`` field directly;
if OF rejects the cancel (already fired, wrong owner) it bubbles
as an ``OFException`` → the global handler maps it to the right
HTTP status. Our 200/false response means "OF accepted the call
but reported the item couldn't be cancelled" — usually because
it's already in the middle of firing.
(Required) ID of the queued message to cancel.

Post a new story.

Per-item dispatch (mirrors upstream's ``post_story`` polymorphism
but expressed as a typed contract):

* ``url``       → uploaded first and referenced via
                  processId/host/name/extra. Our server downloads the
                  file directly (Drive/Dropbox share links work); only
                  OnlyFans' own links go through the account's proxy.
* ``uploadId``  → reuse a previously-uploaded S3 file directly
                  (no second upload).
* ``mediaId``   → reference an existing vault Media item by id.

We call upstream's ``client.http.post_story(media_files)`` directly
instead of ``client.post_story(media)`` so we don't pay the upload
twice for the ``uploadId`` case — the upstream wrapper only knows
how to handle live S3File / Media Python objects, not the wire
shape we ship back to customers via ``/uploads``.

Start an upload for a file too large for one request.

The edge rejects request bodies over 100 MB, so a large video is sent
in parts:

1. ``POST /uploads/chunked`` with the file's ``sizeBytes``. The response
   has the upload ``id``, ``partSize`` and ``partCount``.
2. ``PUT /uploads/{id}/parts/{n}`` for n = 1..partCount. Part n is bytes
   ``(n-1)*partSize`` to ``n*partSize`` of the file (the last part holds
   the remainder). Parts can go in any order or in parallel; a failed
   part is simply sent again.
3. ``POST /uploads/{id}/complete``. The OnlyFans upload then runs in the
   background; poll ``GET /uploads/{id}`` until ``completed`` and use its
   ``media`` like the response of ``POST /uploads``.

An upload that isn't completed within 24 hours is discarded.
